problem: The trap says the sequence CNOT(2→1), CNOT(1→2), CNOT(2→1) is a common wrong answer that does not swap. That sequence does swap: on (a, b) it gives (a⊕b, b), then (a⊕b, a), then (b, a). It is the same circuit as the listed order with the two qubit names exchanged. A student who checks it will find it works, so the trap teaches a false rule.
fix: Two CNOTs in opposite directions do not swap. You need three, and the middle one must point opposite to the other two: 1→2, 2→1, 1→2 swaps, and so does 2→1, 1→2, 2→1 (the same circuit with the qubit labels exchanged). Three CNOTs all pointing the same way do not swap.

problem: The note on the middle gate reads 'b⊕(a⊕b)=a', but the value produced by that gate is on qubit 1 and equals a⊕(a⊕b)=b. The expression shown belongs to the third gate, so the chain of intermediate values in the figure is inconsistent with the text.
fix: Change the c2 note to 'a⊕(a⊕b)=b' and the c3 note to '(a⊕b)⊕b=a'.
